refinedSections.title: 1. Protocol Summary
refinedSections.summary: Contains the synopsis, schema, and schedule of activities providing an executive overview of the entire clinical protocol including study objectives, design, and assessment timeline.

refinedSections.title: 1.1 Synopsis
refinedSections.summary: Executive summary of the protocol including title, sponsor, protocol number, phase, brief title, regulatory identifiers, objectives, endpoints, design synopsis, and brief summary description.

refinedSections.title: 1.2 Schema
refinedSections.summary: Visual representation or tabular format showing the study design structure, arms, interventions, and participant flow through the study periods.

refinedSections.title: 1.3 Schedule of Activities (SoA)
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive timeline matrix showing all study activities, assessments, and procedures across all visits and timepoints from screening through follow-up.

refinedSections.title: 2. Introduction
refinedSections.summary: Provides scientific background and justification for the study including study rationale, disease background, and benefit-risk assessment.

refinedSections.title: 2.1 Study Rationale
refinedSections.summary: Scientific and clinical justification for conducting the study, explaining the medical need and knowledge gap this trial addresses.

refinedSections.title: 2.2 Background
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive review of relevant disease information, current treatment landscape, and prior research supporting this study.

refinedSections.title: 2.3 Benefit/Risk Assessment
refinedSections.summary: Evaluation of the potential benefits versus risks of the study intervention for the target population.

refinedSections.title: 2.3.1 Risk Assessment
refinedSections.summary: Detailed analysis of potential safety risks, adverse events, and safety mitigation strategies associated with the study intervention.

refinedSections.title: 2.3.2 Benefit Assessment
refinedSections.summary: Evaluation of potential therapeutic benefits and clinical improvements expected from the study intervention.

refinedSections.title: 2.3.3 Overall Benefit Risk Conclusion
refinedSections.summary: Synthesized conclusion weighing the overall benefit-risk profile to justify proceeding with the clinical trial.

refinedSections.title: 3. Objectives, Endpoints, and Estimands
refinedSections.summary: Defines primary, secondary, and exploratory objectives with corresponding endpoints and estimands that specify what will be measured, in which population, and how intercurrent events are handled.

refinedSections.title: 4. Study Design
refinedSections.summary: Detailed description of the overall study design, scientific rationale, dose justification, and end-of-study definition.

refinedSections.title: 4.1 Overall Design
refinedSections.summary: Description of study type (randomized, controlled, parallel-group, crossover, etc.), number of arms, masking/blinding procedures, and study phases.

refinedSections.title: 4.2 Scientific Rationale for Study Design
refinedSections.summary: Justification for the chosen study design based on scientific, clinical, and regulatory considerations.

refinedSections.title: 4.2.1 Patient Input into Design
refinedSections.summary: Description of how patient feedback and perspectives were incorporated into the study design, including patient engagement activities.

refinedSections.title: 4.3 Justification for Dose
refinedSections.summary: Scientific justification for the selected dose(s) and/or dosing regimen based on preclinical, pharmacokinetic, and prior clinical data.

refinedSections.title: 4.4 End-of-Study Definition
refinedSections.summary: Clear definition of when the study ends and when a participant is considered to have completed the study.

refinedSections.title: 1. Protocol Summary
refinedSections.summary: High-level overview of the clinical protocol including title, regulatory identifiers, study rationale, objectives and endpoints in tabular format, overall design synopsis with masking details, brief summary of study purpose and duration, number of participants to be screened and enrolled, study arms and duration, and data monitoring committee information if applicable.

refinedSections.title: 1.1. Synopsis
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive protocol summary table containing protocol title, brief title, regulatory agency identifiers, pediatric investigational plan number, rationale, objectives and endpoints mapped to primary/secondary/tertiary categories, overall design synopsis with masking details, brief summary of study purpose including duration and visit frequency, participant enrollment numbers, study arms with durations, and data monitoring committee details.

refinedSections.title: 1.2. Schema
refinedSections.summary: Visual or tabular representation of the study design flow showing participant progression through screening, randomization, intervention periods, and follow-up phases across different study arms.

refinedSections.title: 1.3. Schedule of Activities (SoA)
refinedSections.summary: Detailed timeline table specifying all study procedures, assessments, and interventions across screening, intervention period (with specific days/weeks), early discontinuation, and follow-up visits, including informed consent, eligibility criteria, demography, physical examinations, medical history, pregnancy testing, laboratory tests, ECGs, vital signs, randomization, and study-specific assessments.

refinedSections.title: 2. Introduction
refinedSections.summary: Provides scientific and clinical context for the study, including study rationale explaining why the investigation is being conducted, background information on the investigational intervention including mechanism of action and development stage, and comprehensive benefit/risk assessment.

refinedSections.title: 2.1. Study Rationale
refinedSections.summary: Explains the scientific and medical justification for conducting the study, including the clinical need, unmet medical need being addressed, and how the investigational intervention may provide benefit.

refinedSections.title: 2.2. Background
refinedSections.summary: Scientific background on the investigational intervention including its pharmacological properties, mechanism of action, development stage, and relevant preclinical or clinical data supporting its investigation. References to investigator's brochure, package insert, or other technical documentation.

refinedSections.title: 2.3. Benefit/Risk Assessment
refinedSections.summary: Overall evaluation of the potential benefits versus risks for study participants, including reference to safety data from investigator's brochure, participant information leaflet, package insert, DSUR, or other sources. Forms the basis for the ethical justification of the study.

refinedSections.title: 2.3.1. Risk Assessment
refinedSections.summary: Detailed assessment of known and potential risks associated with the investigational intervention, including reasonably expected adverse events and measures taken to minimize risk to participants.

refinedSections.title: 2.3.2. Benefit Assessment
refinedSections.summary: Evaluation of anticipated benefits for participants, including potential therapeutic advantages and clinical improvements expected from the investigational intervention.

refinedSections.title: 2.3.3. Overall Benefit Risk Conclusion
refinedSections.summary: Integrated conclusion weighing the potential benefits against the identified risks, justifying why the risks are acceptable in light of anticipated benefits for the target participant population.

refinedSections.title: 3. Objectives, Endpoints, and Estimands
refinedSections.summary: Defines the study objectives organized by primary, secondary, and tertiary/exploratory categories, their corresponding endpoints, and the estimands framework that specifies the population, endpoint, interventions, and intercurrent event strategies for each objective.

refinedSections.title: 4. Study Design
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive description of the study methodology including overall design type, scientific justification for the design choices, dose selection rationale, patient input into design considerations, and clear definition of when the study ends for individual participants and the study as a whole.

refinedSections.title: 4.1. Overall Design
refinedSections.summary: Description of the study design type (e.g., randomized, controlled, parallel-group, crossover, dose-ranging), number of arms, phase of development, masking strategy, and general methodological approach.

refinedSections.title: 4.2. Scientific Rationale for Study Design
refinedSections.summary: Justification for why this specific study design was chosen, including reference to regulatory guidance, statistical considerations, and scientific principles. May include patient input into design.

refinedSections.title: 4.3. Justification for Dose
refinedSections.summary: Rationale for selection of the dose(s) to be studied, including reference to preclinical data, previous clinical studies, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic data, and safety considerations. For dose-escalation designs, includes criteria for moving between dose levels.

refinedSections.title: 4.4. End-of-Study Definition
refinedSections.summary: Clear definition of when individual participants are considered to have completed the study and when the overall study is considered ended (e.g., last visit of last participant globally).

refinedSections.title: 5. Study Population
refinedSections.summary: Detailed criteria defining who can participate in the study, organized into inclusion criteria (who may participate) and exclusion criteria (who may not participate), covering demographic characteristics, disease status, medical conditions, prior therapies, and lifestyle considerations.

refinedSections.title: 5.1. Inclusion Criteria
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive list of criteria that participants must meet to be eligible for the study, organized by categories including age requirements, type of participant and disease characteristics, weight/BMI requirements, sex and contraceptive/barrier requirements, informed consent, and other protocol-specific criteria.

refinedSections.title: 5.2. Exclusion Criteria
refinedSections.summary: List of criteria that disqualify potential participants from study enrollment, organized by categories including medical conditions, liver safety considerations, prior/concomitant therapy restrictions, prior/concurrent clinical study experience, diagnostic assessment findings, and other exclusion criteria.

refinedSections.title: 5.3. Lifestyle Considerations
refinedSections.summary: Requirements and restrictions related to participant lifestyle during the study, including meals and dietary restrictions (e.g., grapefruit, Seville oranges), caffeine, alcohol, and tobacco restrictions, activity limitations, and other protocol-specific restrictions.

refinedSections.title: 5.4. Screen Failures
refinedSections.summary: Guidance on handling participants who consent but fail screening, including documentation requirements (demographics, screen failure details, eligibility criteria, SAEs) and whether rescreening is permitted with new participant numbers.

refinedSections.title: 5.5. Criteria for Temporarily Delaying Enrollment/Randomization/Administration
refinedSections.summary: Criteria under which enrollment, randomization, or administration of study intervention may be temporarily delayed, typically based on safety findings, abnormal laboratory values, or other clinical considerations.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 5.5. Criteria for Temporarily Delaying Enrollment/Randomization/Administration of Study Intervention

refinedSections.title: 6. Study Intervention(s) and Concomitant Therapy
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive information about all investigational and non-investigational interventions administered in the study, including detailed descriptions of study interventions, preparation and handling, assignment procedures, blinding/masking methods, compliance monitoring, dose modifications, continued access provisions, overdose management, and prior/concomitant therapy restrictions.

refinedSections.title: 6.1. Study Intervention(s) Administered
refinedSections.summary: Detailed description of all study interventions including investigational medicinal products (IMPs), non-investigational medicinal products (NIMPs), additional medicinal products (AxMPs), rescue medicine, and medical devices, with information on formulation, dosage, route of administration, packaging, and labeling.

refinedSections.title: 6.2. Preparation, Handling, Storage, and Accountability
refinedSections.summary: Instructions for preparation of study interventions prior to administration, proper handling procedures, storage conditions (temperature, light sensitivity, shelf life), and accountability procedures for tracking intervention dispensing and returns.

refinedSections.title: 6.3. Assignment to Study Intervention
refinedSections.summary: Description of how participants are assigned to study interventions, including randomization procedures (method, stratification factors), allocation ratio, and implementation of the assignment process.

refinedSections.title: 6.4. Blinding/Masking
refinedSections.summary: Description of blinding procedures including who is blinded (participants, investigators, assessors, caregivers), methods for maintaining blinding (identical appearance, double-dummy techniques), procedures for emergency unblinding, and assessment of blinding success.

refinedSections.title: 6.5. Study Intervention Compliance
refinedSections.summary: Methods for monitoring and assessing participant compliance with study intervention administration, including timing of doses, missed doses, procedures for documenting compliance (e.g., diaries, pill counts, drug level monitoring), and thresholds for acceptable compliance.

refinedSections.title: 6.6. Dose Modification
refinedSections.summary: Circumstances under which dose modifications may be made (e.g., toxicity, intolerance), specific protocols for dose reductions or interruptions, criteria for retreatment, and documentation requirements for any dose modifications.

refinedSections.title: 6.7. Continued Access to Study Intervention after the End of the Study
refinedSections.summary: Provisions for participants to continue receiving study intervention after study completion, including extension studies, compassionate use programs, or other mechanisms for continued access.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 6.7. Continued Access to Study Intervention after the End of the Study

refinedSections.title: 6.8. Treatment of Overdose
refinedSections.summary: Procedures for managing overdose of study intervention, including signs and symptoms of overdose, immediate management steps, recommended treatments or antidotes if available, and reporting requirements for overdose events.

refinedSections.title: 6.9. Prior and Concomitant Therapy
refinedSections.summary: Restrictions and guidance regarding medications and therapies that participants may receive before or during the study, including prohibited medications, allowed concomitant medications with timing restrictions, washout periods, and procedures for documenting concomitant medication use.

refinedSections.title: 7. Discontinuation of Study Intervention and Participant Discontinuation/Withdrawal
refinedSections.summary: Procedures and criteria for discontinuing study intervention (including organ-specific stopping criteria for liver events and QTc prolongation, temporary discontinuation, and rechallenge protocols) and for participant withdrawal from the study, including handling of lost to follow-up participants.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 7. Discontinuation of Study Intervention and Participant Discontinuation/Withdrawal

refinedSections.title: 7.1. Discontinuation of Study Intervention
refinedSections.summary: Criteria and procedures for permanently or temporarily discontinuing study intervention, including specific stopping rules for liver events and QTc prolongation, protocols for temporary discontinuation, and criteria for rechallenging participants after discontinuation.

refinedSections.title: 7.2. Participant Discontinuation/Withdrawal from the Study
refinedSections.summary: Procedures for handling participant withdrawal from the study, including voluntary withdrawal, withdrawal due to adverse events or protocol violations, procedures for obtaining data from participants who discontinue, and documentation requirements.

refinedSections.title: 7.3. Lost to Follow up
refinedSections.summary: Procedures for handling participants who are lost to follow-up, including attempts to contact, documentation requirements, and implications for data collection and safety monitoring.

refinedSections.title: 8. Study Assessments and Procedures
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive description of all assessments and procedures performed during the study, including administrative procedures, efficacy and immunogenicity assessments, safety assessments (physical exams, vital signs, ECGs, laboratory tests, pregnancy testing, suicidal ideation monitoring), adverse event reporting, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic assessments, genetics, biomarkers, and health economics evaluations.

refinedSections.title: 8.1. Administrative Procedures
refinedSections.summary: Administrative and general procedures including informed consent documentation, eligibility assessments, screening log maintenance, and procedures for utilizing routine clinical management data for study purposes when obtained within specified timeframes.

refinedSections.title: 8.2. Efficacy and/or Immunogenicity Assessments
refinedSections.summary: Detailed description of efficacy endpoint measurements including specific assessments, instruments or scales used, timing of assessments, methods of administration, quality control procedures, and criteria for meaningful change or response. For immunogenicity studies, includes antibody testing methods and interpretation criteria.

refinedSections.title: 8.3. Safety Assessments
refinedSections.summary: Overview of all safety monitoring performed in the study, with detailed subsections covering physical examinations, vital signs, electrocardiograms, clinical laboratory tests, pregnancy testing, and suicidal ideation/behavior risk monitoring including specific methodologies, timing, and criteria for clinical significance.

refinedSections.title: 8.4. Adverse Events (AEs) Serious Adverse Events (SAEs), and Other Safety Reporting
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive adverse event reporting framework including definitions, time periods for collection, methods of detection, follow-up procedures, regulatory reporting requirements for SAEs, pregnancy reporting, cardiovascular and death event reporting, disease-related events not qualifying as AEs/SAEs, adverse events of special interest, and medical device deficiencies.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 8.4. Adverse Events (AEs) Serious Adverse Events (SAEs), and Other Safety Reporting

refinedSections.title: 8.5. Pharmacokinetics
refinedSections.summary: Description of pharmacokinetic assessments including sampling schedule, sample type (e.g., plasma, serum), sampling methods, analytes measured, analytical methods, PK parameters to be estimated (e.g., Cmax, Tmax, AUC, half-life), and special considerations such as timing relative to dosing and food effects.

refinedSections.title: 8.6. Pharmacodynamics
refinedSections.summary: Description of pharmacodynamic assessments including the relationship between drug concentration and pharmacological effect, biomarkers used to assess pharmacodynamic response, timing of assessments, and methods for measuring and interpreting pharmacodynamic effects.

refinedSections.title: 8.7. Genetics
refinedSections.summary: Description of genetic assessments including the purpose of genetic testing (e.g., pharmacogenomics, biomarker identification), specific genetic variants or genes being analyzed, sample collection and processing methods, storage procedures, and confidentiality considerations for genetic information.

refinedSections.title: 8.8. Biomarkers
refinedSections.summary: Description of biomarker assessments including the specific biomarkers being measured, their relevance to the study (e.g., predictive, prognostic, pharmacodynamic), sample collection and processing methods, analytical methods, timing of assessments, and interpretation criteria.

refinedSections.title: 8.9. Immunogenicity Assessments
refinedSections.summary: Description of immunogenicity testing for biologic interventions including assessment of anti-drug antibodies, neutralizing antibodies, sampling schedule, assay methodology, interpretation of immunogenicity results, and potential impact on safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics.

refinedSections.title: 8.10. Health Economics OR Medical Resource Utilization and Health Economics
refinedSections.summary: Description of health economics assessments including medical resource utilization tracking (e.g., hospitalizations, physician visits, concomitant medications), quality of life measures, cost-effectiveness analyses, and instruments used to capture economic and utilization data.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 8.10. [Health Economics OR Medical Resource Utilization and Health Economics]

refinedSections.title: 9. Statistical Considerations
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive section describing the statistical methodology for analyzing study data, including general considerations, decision criteria and statistical hypotheses, multiplicity adjustments, intercurrent event strategies, handling of missing data, analysis sets, detailed analysis methods for primary/secondary/exploratory objectives, safety analyses, subgroup analyses, interim analyses, and sample size determination.

refinedSections.title: 9.1. General Considerations
refinedSections.summary: Overview of statistical analysis principles including when the statistical analysis plan will be finalized, general analysis approach (e.g., intent-to-treat vs. per-protocol), significance levels, confidence intervals, and software to be used for analyses.

refinedSections.title: 9.2. Analysis Sets
refinedSections.summary: Definition of analysis populations including the set of participants considered for analysis (e.g., all participants as randomized, all who received intervention, all who had post-baseline assessments), criteria for inclusion in each analysis set, and handling of protocol deviations.

refinedSections.title: 9.3. Analyses Supporting Primary Objective(s)
refinedSections.summary: Detailed description of statistical methods for analyzing primary objectives including endpoint definitions, main analytical approaches (e.g., ANCOVA, logistic regression, survival analysis), sensitivity analyses, supplementary analyses, and presentation of results.

refinedSections.title: 9.4. Analyses Supporting Secondary Objective(s)
refinedSections.summary: Statistical methods for analyzing secondary objectives, organized by each secondary objective with specific descriptions of endpoint definitions and analytical approaches for each secondary analysis.

refinedSections.title: 9.5. Analyses Supporting Tertiary/Exploratory/Other Objective(s)
refinedSections.summary: Statistical methods for analyzing tertiary, exploratory, or other objectives, noting that these analyses may be descriptive or hypothesis-generating and may be subject to different interpretation criteria than primary and secondary analyses.

refinedSections.title: 9.6. Other Safety Analyses
refinedSections.summary: Description of safety data analysis methods including summary tables of adverse events, laboratory abnormalities, vital signs, ECG findings, and other safety parameters. May include specific analyses for safety subsets or special safety populations.

refinedSections.title: 9.7. Other Analyses
refinedSections.summary: Description of additional analyses not covered in primary, secondary, or exploratory objectives, including other variables and parameters of interest and planned subgroup analyses with descriptions of subgroup factors and rationale for subgroup evaluations.

refinedSections.title: 9.8. Interim Analyses
refinedSections.summary: Description of any planned interim analyses including their purpose (e.g., safety monitoring, efficacy assessment, futility analysis), timing, who will have access to interim results, impact on final analyses, and any stopping rules or guidelines for study continuation based on interim results.

refinedSections.title: 9.9. Sample Size Determination
refinedSections.summary: Detailed justification of the sample size including the primary endpoint used for sample size calculation, assumed treatment effect, variability, significance level, power, dropout rate assumptions, and any adjustments for multiple comparisons or non-inferiority margins.

refinedSections.title: 10. Supporting Documentation and Operational Considerations
refinedSections.summary: Collection of appendices providing detailed operational guidance, regulatory and ethical considerations, clinical laboratory reference ranges, detailed adverse event definitions and reporting procedures, contraceptive guidance, genetics procedures, liver safety guidelines, medical device adverse event reporting, country-specific requirements, and protocol amendment history.

refinedSections.title: 10.1. Appendix 1: Regulatory, Ethical, and Study Oversight Considerations
refinedSections.summary: Comprehensive appendix covering regulatory and ethical compliance (Declaration of Helsinki, GCP guidelines, IRB/IEC requirements), financial disclosure requirements, informed consent process and documentation, recruitment strategy, data protection and privacy measures, committee structure (e.g., DMC, EC), dissemination plans, data quality assurance, source documentation, study start-up and closure procedures, and publication policy.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 10.1. Appendix 1: Regulatory, Ethical, and Study Oversight Considerations

refinedSections.title: 10.2. Appendix 2: Clinical Laboratory Tests
refinedSections.summary: Reference information for clinical laboratory tests including normal ranges, units of measurement, and specific assays or methodologies used. May include hematology, chemistry, coagulation, urinalysis, and other laboratory parameters with protocol-specific criteria for clinical significance.

refinedSections.title: 10.3. Appendix 3: AEs and SAEs Definitions and Procedures
refinedSections.summary: Detailed definitions and operational procedures for adverse event and serious adverse event recording, evaluation, follow-up, and regulatory reporting. Includes specific definitions of AEs and SAEs with examples, intensity grading scales, causality assessment methods, timelines for reporting, and special considerations for pregnancy, cardiovascular events, and medical device studies.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 10.3. Appendix 3: AEs and SAEs: Definitions and Procedures for Recording, Evaluating, Follow-up, and Reporting

refinedSections.title: 10.4. Appendix 4: Contraceptive and Barrier Guidance
refinedSections.summary: Detailed guidance on contraceptive and barrier method requirements for study participants, including definitions of highly effective contraception, specific requirements for male and female participants, duration requirements, permitted and prohibited methods, and verification procedures.

refinedSections.title: 1. List of Abbreviations and Definitions of Terms

refinedSections.title: 2. Synopsis
refinedSections.summary: High-level overview of the trial design, objectives, patient population, endpoints, treatment schedule, and key study parameters for the Phase 1b/2a trial of Sym004 in combination with FOLFIRI.

refinedSections.title: 3. Background and Rationale
refinedSections.summary: Scientific and clinical context for the trial including disease background, current treatments, investigational product characteristics, trial rationale, and benefit/risk assessment.

refinedSections.title: 3.1 Disease and Treatment
refinedSections.summary: Overview of metastatic colorectal cancer epidemiology, staging, survival rates, and current treatment landscape including EGFR-targeted therapies.

refinedSections.title: 3.1.1 Metastatic Colorectal Cancer
refinedSections.summary: Epidemiology and survival statistics for colorectal cancer by stage, with focus on Stage IV metastatic disease (12% five-year survival).

refinedSections.title: 3.1.2 Current Treatment of Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Disease
refinedSections.summary: Standard of care regimens including FOLFIRI, anti-EGFR antibodies (cetuximab, panitumumab), and RAS mutation status as a biomarker for treatment response.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 3.1.2 Current Treatment of Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Disease

refinedSections.title: 3.2 Investigational Medicinal Product
refinedSections.summary: Description of Sym004 composition, mechanism of action, non-clinical findings, and summary of clinical safety, pharmacokinetics, and efficacy data.

refinedSections.title: 3.2.1 Sym004
refinedSections.summary: Sym004 is a 1:1 mixture of two chimeric IgG1 monoclonal antibodies (futuximab and modotuximab) targeting non-overlapping EGFR epitopes.

refinedSections.title: 3.2.2 Mechanism of Action
refinedSections.summary: Sym004 induces EGFR internalization and degradation through dual epitope binding, demonstrating superior activity versus single-agent anti-EGFR antibodies including in cetuximab-resistant cells.

refinedSections.title: 3.2.3 Summary of Non-clinical Findings
refinedSections.summary: In vitro and in vivo studies showing superior EGFR downregulation and anti-tumor activity versus cetuximab/panitumumab, with toxicology profile consistent with anti-EGFR class effects.

refinedSections.title: 3.2.4 Summary of Clinical Findings
refinedSections.summary: Clinical experience with Sym004 across multiple tumor types including safety, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and antitumor efficacy data.

refinedSections.title: 3.2.4.1 Safety
refinedSections.summary: Safety profile from 175+ patients treated with Sym004 at various doses and schedules, documenting tolerability and adverse event patterns.

refinedSections.title: 3.2.4.2 Pharmacokinetics
refinedSections.summary: PK characteristics of Sym004 administration including dose-proportionality and exposure parameters.

refinedSections.title: 3.2.4.3 Pharmacodynamic Effects
refinedSections.summary: Biomarker and mechanistic assessments of Sym004 biological activity in clinical studies.

refinedSections.title: 3.2.4.4 Antitumor Effects
refinedSections.summary: Objective response rates and disease control observed with Sym004 monotherapy and combination therapy across tumor types.

refinedSections.title: 3.3 Trial Rationale
refinedSections.summary: Justification for evaluating Sym004 in combination with FOLFIRI in RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer patients.

refinedSections.title: 3.4 Dose Rationale
refinedSections.summary: Scientific basis for starting dose selection and dose-escalation scheme based on prior clinical experience.

refinedSections.title: 3.5 Overall Benefit/Risk
refinedSections.summary: Assessment of potential benefits versus known and anticipated risks for trial participants.

refinedSections.title: 4. Trial Objectives and Endpoints
refinedSections.summary: Primary and secondary objectives for dose-escalation and dose-expansion phases, with corresponding endpoints for safety, efficacy, PK, and biomarker assessments.

refinedSections.title: 4.1 Dose-Escalation (Phase 1b)
refinedSections.summary: Objectives for the dose-escalation phase focused on determining maximum tolerated dose and recommended Phase 2 dose.

refinedSections.title: 4.1.1 Primary Objective
refinedSections.summary: To determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and/or recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D) of Sym004 in combination with FOLFIRI.

refinedSections.title: 4.1.2 Secondary Objectives
refinedSections.summary: Assess safety, tolerability, antitumor activity, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of Sym004 plus FOLFIRI during dose-escalation.

refinedSections.title: 4.2 Dose-Expansion (Phase 2a)
refinedSections.summary: Objectives for dose-expansion phase evaluating antitumor activity and further safety characterization at the RP2D.

refinedSections.title: 4.2.1 Primary Objective
refinedSections.summary: To assess confirmed objective antitumor response to Sym004 at RP2D in combination with FOLFIRI.

refinedSections.title: 4.2.2 Secondary Objectives
refinedSections.summary: Further evaluate safety, tolerability, duration of response, progression-free survival, and overall survival during dose-expansion.

refinedSections.title: 4.3 Exploratory Studies
refinedSections.summary: Biomarker analyses including RAS mutation profiling, anti-drug antibodies, and other translational research endpoints.

refinedSections.title: 4.4 Trial Endpoints
refinedSections.summary: Detailed definitions of primary and secondary endpoints for both trial phases.

refinedSections.title: 4.4.1 Primary Endpoint of Dose-Escalation (Phase 1b)
refinedSections.summary: Occurrence of dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) during Cycle 1 of Sym004 plus FOLFIRI administration.

refinedSections.title: 4.4.2 Primary Endpoint of Dose-Expansion Phase (Phase 2a)
refinedSections.summary: Confirmed objective antitumor response (complete or partial response) per RECIST v1.1 criteria.

refinedSections.title: 4.4.3 Secondary Endpoints of Dose-Escalation and Dose-Expansion Phases
refinedSections.summary: Safety, antitumor response metrics, pharmacokinetic parameters, and biomarker assessments across both phases.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 4.4.3 Secondary Endpoints of Dose-Escalation and Dose-Expansion Phases

refinedSections.title: 4.4.3.1 Safety
refinedSections.summary: Adverse events, laboratory abnormalities, vital signs, ECG findings, and other safety parameters throughout treatment.

refinedSections.title: 4.4.3.2 Anti-tumor Response
refinedSections.summary: Best overall response, duration of response, disease control rate, progression-free survival, and overall survival.

refinedSections.title: 4.4.3.3 Pharmacokinetic Assessment (Dose-Escalation only)
refinedSections.summary: PK parameters for both antibody components of Sym004 during dose-escalation phase (omitted as of Amendment 3).

refinedSections.title: 4.4.3.4 Pharmacodynamic and Biomarker Assessment
refinedSections.summary: Anti-drug antibody formation and exploratory biomarker analyses from blood, urine, and tumor samples (omitted as of Amendment 3).

refinedSections.title: 5. Trial Design
refinedSections.summary: Overall study design including dose-escalation and dose-expansion phases, schedule of events, patient numbers, and trial duration.

refinedSections.title: 5.1 Overall Design and Plan
refinedSections.summary: Phase 1b/2a open-label multi-center trial design with 3+3 dose-escalation followed by expansion at RP2D, treating up to 50 patients total.

refinedSections.title: 5.2 Discussion of Trial Design
refinedSections.summary: Rationale for design choices including patient population, starting dose, route of administration, and escalation/expansion strategy.

refinedSections.title: 5.2.1 Rationale for Trial Design
refinedSections.summary: Justification for the Phase 1b/2a adaptive design with dose-escalation to identify optimal dosing.

refinedSections.title: 5.2.2 Rationale for Trial Population
refinedSections.summary: Selection of RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer patients who failed first-line oxaliplatin-based therapy.

refinedSections.title: 5.2.3 Rationale for Starting Dose and Route of Administration
refinedSections.summary: Scientific basis for 12 mg/kg as starting dose and intravenous infusion as route based on prior clinical data.
refinedSections.originalHeading: 5.2.3 Rationale for Starting Dose and Route of Administration

refinedSections.title: 5.2.4 Rationale for Dose-Escalation and Dose-Expansion
refinedSections.summary: Justification for 3+3 escalation design and expansion cohort size to assess both safety and preliminary efficacy.

refinedSections.summary: Detailed timeline of screening, treatment, and follow-up visits with assessment schedules.

refinedSections.title: 5.4 Recruitment Period
refinedSections.summary: Expected duration of patient enrollment period for the trial.

refinedSections.title: 5.5 Number of Patients
refinedSections.summary: Planned enrollment of approximately 50 patients across dose-escalation (9-18 patients) and dose-expansion (32-41 patients) phases.

refinedSections.title: 5.6 End of Trial
refinedSections.summary: Definition of trial completion and criteria for trial termination.

refinedSections.summary: Eligibility criteria (inclusion/exclusion), withdrawal procedures, and patient replacement rules for both trial phases.

refinedSections.title: 6.1 Inclusion Criteria All Cohorts
refinedSections.summary: Patients must have RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer, failed first-line oxaliplatin therapy, ECOG PS 0-1, measurable disease, and adequate organ function.

refinedSections.title: 6.2 Exclusion Criteria All Cohorts
refinedSections.summary: Exclusions include prior EGFR-targeted therapy, brain metastases, significant cardiac disease, active infections, and inadequate washout from prior treatments.

refinedSections.summary: Criteria and procedures for discontinuing Sym004 and/or FOLFIRI or complete withdrawal from the trial.

refinedSections.title: 7.2.3 Prophylactic Treatment
refinedSections.summary: Mandatory prophylaxis protocols for infusion reactions, gastrointestinal toxicities (diarrhea), and skin toxicities.

refinedSections.title: 7.2.4 Treatment of Skin Toxicity
refinedSections.summary: Graded management algorithms for EGFR inhibitor-related skin toxicities including rash, xerosis, paronychia, pruritus, photosensitivity, and fissures.
